chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: Hammond bass on records
summary: Organ bass lacks definition, so players fill in; conflicts with a bass player's line.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now, the bass of the Hammond, that didn't record well, did it?
I mean, on a lot of records they use a regular bass player.
Well, it doesn't have the definition that a Fender would have, see. But it records well if you use the amp?
Well, why didn't more people use the amp?
Well, you use the bass to fill it out, to punctuate a certain thing, and then you go back on the (?).
Only certain organs have that bass tone, the dominant bass tone. If you were using that in conjunction
with a bass, you have to play through his bass line.
Well, I thought when they had a regular bass player they didn't play the organ bass.
That's right. Well, it conflicts. It's a conflict.
